script: Spread and total were not saved for NYJ at CHI, so this is form-only: the Bears should stay on the ground with D.Swift (54 carries, 253 yards) and K.Monangai (30 carries, 178 yards), while the Jets have to throw because B.Hall (51/163) and B.Allen (19/61) are both at 3.2 YPC and G.Wilson already has 28 targets for 243 yards into a CHI defense allowing 5.09 YPC.
who_goes_off: Against the Jets, CHI's K.Raymond should go off as the volume receiver (21 targets, 214 yards, 10.2 yards per target) and D.Swift as the Bears' touch leader at 84.3 rush yards per game; for NYJ, G.Wilson (81.0 receiving yards per game, 284 air yards) is the Jet built to attack the Bears' middle.
weak_spot: The Bears' hole versus the Jets is the run (CHI allows 5.09 YPC and 9 runs of 10+) plus the middle (8.42 YPA on 19 attempts) and the right (8.24 YPA on 33 attempts); the Jets' hole versus the Bears is the middle (NYJ allows 7.82 YPA on 22 attempts), while NYJ's right is sound at 4.78 YPA on 37 attempts and NYJ has allowed only 4 passes of 20+ on 101 attempts.
injury_fallout: No injury report was saved for NYJ at CHI, so there is no absence-driven redistribution: Jets B.Hall still has 51 carries to B.Allen's 19, and the Bears remain a D.Swift/K.Monangai split at 54 and 30 carries rather than a one-back game created by an injury.
qb_vs_blitz: The Bears blitz at 42% and the Jets QB is better into it (0.29 EPA per dropback on 30 blitz snaps vs 0.17 with no blitz), which supports NYJ's G.Wilson and K.Sadiq (14 targets, 143 yards); the Jets blitz at 35% and the Bears QB is the sharper blitz beater (0.37 EPA on 56 blitz dropbacks vs 0.08 with no blitz), so NYJ heat should feed CHI's K.Raymond and L.Burden (23 targets, 156 yards) instead of stalling the Bears.

picks.why: CHI's K.Raymond has 21 targets and 214 yards in three games (71.3 per game) against a 31.5 line, and the Jets' middle at 7.82 YPA is the soft spot while NYJ's 35% blitz rate runs into a Bears QB at 0.37 EPA versus pressure.

CHI's D.Swift has 54 carries for 253 yards (84.3 per game) versus a 64.5 line, and the Jets have allowed 4.40 YPC with only 6 runs of 10+, not enough NYJ resistance to erase a 20-yard cushion on the Bears' lead back.
